display.title: Shabbos Chazak: The One Time We Shout in Shul
display.summary_short: We never shout in shul, except when Chumash Bereishis is finished and everyone calls out 'Chazak, chazak, v'nischazek!' Uncle Yossi explains why, and the children practice it.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for Shabbos Chazak, the Shabbos of Parshas Vayechi. Quoting Shlomo HaMelech, 'there is a time for everything', Uncle Yossi asks when there could be a time to shout in shul. A shul is Hashem's house of prayer, so we keep it clean, behave our best and say every word of davening carefully, never calling out. But this Shabbos, when the reader finishes the last sedra of Chumash Bereishis, the whole shul, young and old, calls out at the top of their voices 'Chazak, chazak, v'nischazek', asking Hashem for more strength to learn more Torah. Little children like to add 'My mommy baked a chocolate cake', which is not part of the custom, though a child who honors his parents may well get one. Hashem will answer the call and give strength to learn more Torah. The clip ends with everyone practicing the three words together.
display.lesson: Finishing a part of the Torah is a celebration; ask Hashem for strength to learn even more.

date.note: Cut from episode 356 (dated 12-20-88); 'this coming Shabbos' is the end of Bereishis (Vayechi 5749).

sources_cited.note: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer', quoted as Hashem's words.
